recipes.name: Orange Meringue Pie
ingredients_raw: 4 tablespoons butter or margarine, cut into pieces

steps.text: Preheat oven to 400 degrees F (205 degrees C). Line pastry with aluminum foil and a layer of pie weights or dried beans. Bake in the preheated oven until edge of crust is golden, about 10 minutes. Carefully remove the foil and weights; bake about 5 minutes more.

In a small saucepan, stir together the 3/4 cup sugar, 1/3 cup cornstarch, and salt. Mix in the orange juice, lemon juice, and water. Whisk in the egg yolks. Cook over medium heat, stirring frequently, until thick and bubbly, about 5 minutes. Remove from heat, and stir in butter and orange zest. If desired; stir in diced orange segments. Pour into prepared pie crust, cover with plastic wrap, and set aside to cool.

When pie filling has cooled to room temperature, preheat oven and prepare meringue. Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). In a large glass or metal bowl, beat egg whites until foamy. Gradually add 1/2 cup sugar and cream of tartar, continuing to beat until stiff peaks form. Lift your beater or whisk straight up: the egg whites should form a sharp peak that holds its shape. Spread over pie, making sure the meringue completely covers the filling and meets the edges of the pie crust.
Bake in preheated oven until meringue topping is golden brown, about 15 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Orange Meringue Pie
raw_recipe.description: A nice change from lemon meringue, the flavor comes from a generous amount of orange juice and orange zest as well as some segments of fresh orange.

video.description: This orange meringue pie is an incredible (and easy!) dessert recipe to make at home—especially if you're tired of lemon meringue pie and looking to switch it up. The super-fluffy meringue is the perfect match for the zesty, citrusy pie filling.

review.reviewBody: I can't believe that there really is just one review at this delicious pie ... It's the best citrus pie i ever had, better than the Lemon & Lime pie! Thank you very much! I'll make this one again!

This is a fantastic pie. I will admit to two minor changes though...I omitted the water and increased the orange juice to 1.25 cups. I made it this past Saturday as one of five pies that I took to a party. My "theme" for the pies was that they all had to be a flavor I had never had, or made, before... and orange fit the bill perfectly. I expected it to be "ok"... but it was head and shoulders above that mark! I made another today for the family and they loved it. Thank you for the recipe! Just came back to say that I made another one today...it's that good! This one is also delicious. I made another slight change though and cut the lemon juice to 1/3 cup. This pie is absolutely on the favorites list here!

The flavor of the pie was great. However, I am giving it only four stars because the meringue did not adhere to the filling, and that made it impossible to cut slices of this pie. It always fell apart when cut, and so everything then had to be dumped unceremoniously into a bowl. I believe that the direction to allow the filling to cool to room temperature before spreading on the meringue is mistaken. I have read on other websites that it's important to put the meringue on the filling while the filling is still warm, so that the meringue seals the filling and will grip onto the filling, and I believe this to be correct. The fact that I followed this recipe's instruction to allow the filling to cool first is what caused my pie to be impossible to slice. I will make this recipe again because the taste was great, but I will put the meringue on while the filling is warm and I advise anyone else to do the same. Oh, and I put the orange pieces in the filling but I think it would be better without them.

I was pleasantly surprised at how much I enjoyed this pie! I like in-your-face amount of citrus flavor, so I used the juice and zest of three large oranges plus the lemon juice, but no water. Kept sugar the same as the recipe, and it delivered on orange flavor without being sour! I used three whole eggs for the filling and then put whipped cream on top instead of meringue...because I just don't prefer meringue. I'm going to make this for Easter, too!

Delicious pie recipe! My dd wanted some type of orange pie for her b-day and I made this. I did increase sugar to 1 cup and I really enjoyed the flavor. I accidentally misread the recipe and only added 2 Tbsp of butter but next time I will definitely add it. I also added 1/2 teaspoon of vanilla and 1 teaspoon corn starch the meringue. I still got some beads on top but no weeping in the middle. I did make meringue first to make sure filling was hot.

I'm no baker, I restore cars, but love making pies. I made this one and its great, however, next time, I will cut the lemon juice to a 1/4 cup, not a 1/2 cup. I think the pie is slightly too tart. as for the people who said theirs was runny, just make sure you cook it on the stove long enough. Mine was not runny at all, a perfect consistency.

My orange pie is an orange "soup"! The bottom layer of the pie did not set. I followed this recipe very carefully, including step 2, which instructs you to cook the mixture until thick and bubbly "about 5 minutes" on medium heat. At the end of five minutes, mine wasn't at all thick, so I added five more minutes until the mixture had a least thickened a bit, but I mistakenly thought it would set in the oven or when it cooled. NOT SO. Those minutes on the stovetop were the only opportunity to thicken the bottom. Knowing this, I should have waited until the mixture had a good pudding texture, however long that took.

Excellent got raves started on rec. found we did not have orange juice. I used Cara Cara Navel's, crushed them and used all of the pulp to make up the volume with water. Used brown suger to give brown cast to the egg whites. I love pies and I am always looking for some thing different. Thank you

This pie was fantastic. I made it for my dad's birthday, and everyone LOVED it. I made a couple of changes to it, just to make it my own. I used all orange juice, instead of using the 1/2 c lemon juice. I made a graham cracker crust instead of the regular pastry crust. And, because I am not a big fan of meringue, I made a sweetened whipped cream for the top. AWESOME!
Absolutely delicious made with blood oranges instead of regular oranges!!!

Wow, what can I say what a great recipe. I made two of them which was a good thing the first one was gone as soon as my family were allowed to eat it. So have one more for today for dessert and I am sure it will be devoured in the same fashion. I doubled the orange zest though and I did add the orange chunks which is why I think this has to be one of the best pies I have eaten.

The orange flavor was delightful, with more tartness than a lemon pie, especially since lemons don’t seem to have the same punch anymore. The juice came from the most wonderful orange, adding an extra layer of joy to the pie’s flavor.
No changes beginner baker and very first time trying this kind of dessert. I think it may not be perfect but I am still very proud of the accomplishment.
Thank you, Jo, for this great recipe. I made the recipe just as it was written except I used a graham cracker crust and more orange juice than water. It was easy and came out just delicious.
I baked this pie for half an hour and it did not set properly and became watery and inedible. Very disappointed.

My mother used to make this pie, and it was my very favorite! Only she used lemon zest instead of orange zest, fresh orange juice only, and no lemon juice, at all. I'm so glad I found this recipe! It gave me the foundation I needed for her recipe! Thank you, SO much!

This is a nice find! The custard part is delicious. I was afraid it would taste flat, but not at all. Fruity and zingy, but different from lemon pie. The custard was nice and thick (FYI - I chose to omit the orange pieces), but you definitely need to cook it longer than suggested 5 minutes! The meringue was less successful. Tasty and pretty looking, but some major weeping going on (and no, I did not overwhip the egg whites). I will keep the orange custard part for next time, but do a simple, more stable Swiss meringue for the topping.
Family said this was “the best pie we’ve ever had”. ‘Nuf said!
Loved this pie!!! Orange is my favorite flavor!!! Thanks so much for sharing this... 5 🌟 ⭐️💫⭐️🌟ALL THE WAY!!!
Absolutely scrumptious.. Better than lemon meringue pie which I personally find a little to sharp
